title: Cost tests with ambiguous model names must pass model_provider explicitly
answers: cost test picks the wrong provider's price
how to pin pricing in a test for a model name shared by several providers
test for 1hr cache creation pricing flaky across catalogs
body:
Symptom: a pricing test asserts a cost for a model name, but the price comes from another provider's catalog that happens to use a similar or identical model name.
Root cause: when no model_provider is passed, the lookup scans all bundled provider catalogs (see mlflow/utils/providers.py:_list_provider_names), so the matched entry depends on which catalog is found first.
Fix pattern: pass model_provider explicitly in each call that the test compares, e.g. model_provider="anthropic" in tests/tracing/utils/test_utils.py:test_builtin_cost_prices_1hr_cache_creation_higher, for both the baseline and the 1-hour variant so they use the same catalog.
Constraints: apply this in tests that assert specific prices or relative price differences. Tests that only check a cost is not None do not need it.
applies: Tests of builtin cost calculation that depend on a specific provider's pricing.
says: Model pricing tests fail because token costs are checked against the wrong provider catalog.
Automated cost calculation tests report incorrect price amounts for models shared across providers.
Cost verification tests for cache creation fail due to ambiguous provider rate cards.
Ensure pricing tests explicitly select the target provider when comparing model token costs.
search: Builtin cost calculation tests that assert specific prices or relative price differences must pass model_provider explicitly when model names are ambiguous. Without an explicit provider, catalog lookup scans all bundled providers via mlflow/utils/providers.py:_list_provider_names and picks whichever catalog matches first. In tests/tracing/utils/test_utils.py:test_builtin_cost_prices_1hr_cache_creation_higher, both baseline and 1-hour cache variants must pass model_provider='anthropic' to ensure identical catalogs are compared. Tests asserting only that cost is not None do not require an explicit provider.
